title: Route Latency Oracle: KV-cache Impact & Streaming/Sync Delta Panel
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a single dashboard "Oracle Panel" that surfaces model-route latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) with an explicit breakdown of streaming vs synchronous request paths and the observed impact of KV-cache hits vs cold reads. This ticket ties tracing hooks, metric enrichment, and a new aggregator in the metrics pipeline to produce a compact exploratory board for SREs and platform engineers.

Problems we solve:
- Engineers currently lack a clear, single view that isolates latency variance due to KV cache effectiveness vs IO/compute path differences across streaming and non-streaming modes.
- Existing boards are fragmented across multiple dashboards (cohort boards, trace explorers) which slows RCA.
- We need a low-overhead sampling & trace-link pattern that preserves headroom for production traffic while giving high-fidelity latency attribution to cache-hit/miss and streaming boundaries.

Design decisions & scope:
- Dashboard panels: p50/p95/p99 times per model-route, stacked breakdown (kv-hit, kv-miss, kernel-queue, network), and an adjacent streaming vs sync delta view (absolute and % uplift).
- Tracing hooks: add lightweight span tags: "kv_cache.status" (hit/miss), "io.mode" (streaming|sync), "kernel_wait_ms" (numeric), and propagate a short trace_id->metric link to the metrics pipeline.
- Metrics pipeline: new enriched metric series "serve.latency.attr" with labels {model, route, io_mode, kv_status, quantization_profile}. We'll implement a streaming-aware aggregator that performs bucketing for p50/p95/p99 on ingestion to keep storage cost bounded.
- Sampling policy: weighted trace sampling that favors requests with high latency (>95th percentile) + 0.1% uniform baseline; tagged traces will be sampled at higher rate for routes in the active rollout.
- Backwards compatibility: dashboards should fall back to existing latency series if enriched labels are missing (e.g., older runtime versions).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Oracle Panel displays p50/p95/p99 for selected model & route with explicit kv-hit vs kv-miss bands and streaming vs sync delta.
2) Clicking a band links into a filtered trace view (trace explorer) with sampled spans showing kv operations and kernel scheduling.
3) Latency attribution matches offline sampling run (test harness) within 5% for p95.
4) End-to-end pipeline adds <12ms additional overhead to request path when tags are emitted (benchmarked).

Implementation plan & milestones:
- Feb 10–20: Instrument runtime to emit span tags and trace->metric link (ENG runtime PR).
- Feb 21–28: Metrics pipeline aggregator & ingest rule to create enriched "serve.latency.attr" series; implement approximate quantile bucketing on ingestion.
- Mar 01–07: Dashboard panels in Console (query templates, streaming delta visualizations), UX review with SREs.
- Mar 08–12: Trace-sampling policy rollout and trace explorer link integration.
- Mar 13–18: Smoke tests against production traffic using a canary route; verification run vs eval prompt sets.
- Mar 19–20: Ship to prod and monitor for regressions.

Artifacts & links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 (runtime tags + trace link)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1298 (ingest aggregator + bucketing)
- Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/d/latency-oracle/route-kvcache-split (read-only prototype)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Route+Latency+Oracle+Design
- Test harness (offline quantile accuracy): https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-eval/blob/main/kvcache_latency_test.py

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: High-cardinality label explosion (model x route x quantization_profile x kv_status). Mitigation: only materialize quantiles for top N routes by traffic and compact quantiles for tails; use rollout to add labels.
- Risk: Trace sampling could miss rare cold-cache events. Mitigation: add anomaly-triggered burst-sampling when p99 > baseline by X%.
- Risk: Dashboard query cost. Mitigation: pre-aggregate on ingest, cache last-6h views, and bake computed deltas into hourly rollups.

Next steps / blockers:
- Runtime team sign-off for adding span tags (waiting on ENG-314159 review).
- Metrics infra capacity approval for additional ingest cardinality (contact: Priya Singh).

Notes from initial reviews:
- PM review (Ben Holloway): "Great signal separation — ensure the UI allows toggling kv tags for older model families."
- SRE review (Isha Nair): "Prefer conservative sampling; ensure debug-mode can force 100% sampling for a route during investigations."

If anything changes to scope or rollout policy, update this ticket and ping the Observability slack channel (#obs-latency-oracle).
